results.title: Fact Check | Reuters
results.description: Reuters Fact Check addresses online misinformation with coverage that maintains accuracy, integrity and impartiality. The unit is part of Reuters news agency.
results.text:
## Reuters

* Fact Checkcategory ago

  An EU Commission proposal to reinstate a measure that exempts some online platforms from strict privacy rules so they can voluntarily identify, report, and remove child sexual abuse material has been misleadingly described on social media as legislation that would greenlight the bloc itself to scan people's chats.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 20, 2026

  Portsmouth City Council’s fire safety rules, which prohibit objects blocking communal areas in apartment blocks, have been misrepresented online as a ban on England flags due to fears that displays would upset minorities.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 20, 2026

  Eligibility requirements for becoming Britain's prime minister are dictated by political convention, not legislation, meaning an online narrative claiming Andy Burnham cannot legally hold the position is incorrect.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 17, 2026

  A photograph of Lionel Messi and Djed Spence has been altered to falsely suggest the Argentine captain stamped on the England defender's ankle during Argentina's 2-1 World Cup semi-final victory.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 20, 2026

  Cyclosporiasis is caused by a single-celled protozoan parasite that would not be susceptible to the anti-worm drug ivermectin, experts say, contrary to posts from current and former U.S. congresswomen promoting ivermectin in the context of a Cyclospora outbreak affecting 34 states.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 15, 2026

  Bluesky will be included in the UK’s proposed social media ban for under-16s, the government has said, contrary to an online narrative viewed millions of times that claims the app will be exempt.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 14, 2026

  A fake draft of UK legislation has been cited in an online narrative that falsely claims parents can be fined thousands of pounds for failing to supervise their children’s social media use.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 14, 2026

  An old video in which Britain's prime minister-in-waiting Andy Burnham says he was going to a soccer match in a wheelchair to research disabled access has been shortened to misleadingly claim it shows him using the wheelchair to get a better vantage point.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 14, 2026

  Two video clips of traffic lights in Italy and Germany that were warped by fires have been incorrectly described online as showing damage as a direct result of a heatwave in Europe last month.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 14, 2026

  An AI-generated clip depicting a drone light show paying tribute to Portugal forward Cristiano Ronaldo has been re-shared online as authentic footage of his hometown Funchal on the island of Madeira after his very last World Cup match.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 10, 2026

  Years-old conditions for flying flags in England have been misrepresented online as rules that were introduced for the 2026 soccer World Cup.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 10, 2026

  Temperatures in Britain on a day in June 2026 have been incorrectly cited online as the hottest recorded in the country since a heatwave in 1976.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 9, 2026

  An image of the Israeli flag projected onto the Washington Monument was not taken at celebrations of the 250th anniversary of the United States, and the picture is old and likely AI-generated.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 15, 2026

  A fabricated quote attributed to England captain Harry Kane saying he will not wear a rainbow Pride flag in upcoming games because football should not be about “political or social movements” has been shared widely online.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 3, 2026

  There’s no evidence of a petition by German fans to ban African and Muslim players from the national soccer team following Germany’s World Cup elimination, as claimed in posts on social media falsely citing broadcaster Deutsche Welle.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 3, 2026

  An education technology company founded by the son of former British Prime Minister Tony Blair has not been awarded a £100 billion ($134 billion) government contract to develop digital IDs, as has been baselessly claimed online.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 3, 2026

  An old study based on UK Biobank participants which observed that people with higher sunscreen use also had an increased risk of skin cancer has been misrepresented online as suggesting that sunscreen causes skin cancers.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 1, 2026

  Footage of a woman looking away while counting ballot papers has been misleadingly shared online as evidence that the Makerfield by-election was not properly conducted.
* Fact CheckcategoryJune 30, 2026

  Online posts highlighting a study that calculated “cold” weather as causing more deaths than “hotter” conditions miss key context.
* Fact CheckcategoryJuly 3, 2026

  Bristol City Council says it has not threatened to evict residents for flying England flags during the FIFA World Cup, contrary to an online claim that misrepresents the local authority’s flag-flying safety rules.
